reasoning: On the season so far the Pistons are the stronger team; with home court the Pistons start about 10 points better, in a game of about 232 points.
Rest, travel and who is missing tilt it about 3 points towards the Pelicans.
There are psychological storylines, but history says they are worth little here.
Bottom line: the Pistons win 65 times in 100, by about 8; most games like this end between 203 and 251 total points.

analyst.text: Detroit arrive on a high after ending San Antonio's 12-game winning streak on Tuesday, but on the second night of a back-to-back and without Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe. New Orleans are without trade-requester Dejounte Murray (ankle) and Trey Murphy III, and are 1-8 with Murray in the lineup. The angle leans towards Detroit, with fatigue the main counterweight.
